lead_headline: Weekend restaurant sweep nets 4 new leads — Vaultaire, FiNO, and Chick-fil-A debut alongside closures in RiNo and Highlands

restaurant.blurb: 4 leads since Friday: Vaultaire (subterranean HiFi bar beneath La Forêt), FiNO (Mediterranean tapas at renovated All Inn Hotel), Chick-fil-A (drive-thru-only at Central Park), Dumplin' (Highlands closure after 1.5 years).

liquor.blurb: 189 new applications today sustains the week's historic flood at 248 total — the system's largest-ever 7-day haul. Today's batch features Maize Rino (3455 Ringsby Ct, Hotel & Restaurant for Michelin-starred chef Johnny Curiel), Dear Emilia (3615 Delgany St), Olive & Finch's fifth location (1552 E 17th Ave), and Pure Food Inc (1400 Wewatta St). The 248-count represents an 1,081% surge versus last week's 21 filings, confirming Friday-Saturday's deluge wasn't a fluke but rather an ongoing mass renewal or database sync event reshaping April's liquor landscape.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday from Google News RSS holds the 7-day count at 51 across 10 sources — up 13% from last week's 45 and maintaining April's late-month pickup momentum. Instagram (11) edges Facebook (9) as top weekly sources, followed by X.com (7), Reddit (6), and Denver Post (5). Notable weekend coverage included Threads post from Denver Post, Hoodline's Museum of Ice Cream piece, and Facebook buzz about Bottom Creek Brewery. The 51-mention pace confirms media interest has stabilized after Q1's decline, with social platforms anchoring week-over-week growth as April closes.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 since Friday (4 new, 1 canceled) pushes MTD to +32 (+1.2/day) with 90-day net climbing to +137. The weekend's modest gains extend April's late-month rally: the 7-day total now stands at +14 net (26 new, 12 canceled), matching last week's +15 performance and confirming conversions have escaped mid-April's flatline. Recent pattern shows steadier +1-2 daily gains replacing mid-month volatility, though MTD's +1.2/day pace still trails YTD's +1.4/day baseline slightly. Two consecutive strong weeks suggest April could close the gap as month-end approaches.
